purpose: Evaluate exact hierarchical local-wave/global-union MoE top-k as task #20 before the Q3 D1 decode campaign.

candidate.algorithm: Each wave retained its exact local top-k; one wave selected the global top-k over num_waves*top_k value/ID pairs. Lower expert IDs won ties, non-finite values were sanitized for the adversarial gate, slot order and selected-logit softmax order were preserved.
candidate.rollback: Existing iterative whole-block selector remained in the same qwen35_router code object during A/B.
candidate.post_decision: All candidate source, Python policy wiring, env selector, and candidate-only tests were removed after the full-model rejection; git diff against base is empty before this artifact/docs closure.

correctness.standalone: Bit-exact selected IDs and routing-weight F32 bits versus the current selector for 256/512 experts, top-k 1/8/10/16, three rows, adversarial ties, and NaN/Inf inputs after the shared sanitation premise.
correctness.fused_split: Bit-exact logits, IDs, and routing-weight F32 bits at 256 experts/top-k 8/local256.
correctness.development_note: The first implementation failed after top-1 because a shuffle-down winner was valid only in lane 0; broadcasting the winning ID fixed candidate removal before any performance result was accepted.

decision.reason: The production Q3 graph-replay gate regressed decode by 1.15% and prefill by 1.21% despite exact outputs and a faster isolated fused leaf. This triggers task #20's stop rule before 4K, Q4, or PARO expansion.
decision.next: Keep the current iterative selector and use these same-commit off/on controls as D0 evidence. Proceed to task #15 raw-IQ decode attribution and IQ4 down work distribution.
